case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Shyam and others
facts: The respondents were charged of offence punishable u/s. 302 and 201 IPC before the V Additional Sessions Judge, Sitapur who after trial found them guilty of the said offences and sentenced them to undergo imprisonment for life for an offence u/s. 302 read with 34 IPC and further to undergo imprisonment for three years for an offence punishable u/s. 201 IPC.
There was enmity between respondent No.1, Shyam and deceased, Janardhan. The case of the prosecution is that respondent No1. suspected the deceased of having illicit affairs with his wife.
On 11th October, 1978 at about 4 a.m. when the deceased had gone out to answer the call of nature the accused persons attacked him and committed his murder by pressing his neck with lathi.
The said witnesses then with the help of the villagers tried to recover the body of the deceased but they could do so only by about 3 p.m. in the afternoon.
In the meanwhile at 9.30 a.m., PW.8 went to police station Tambaur and lodged a complaint in regard to the incident.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in disbelieving the prosecution case?
petitioner_arguments: The eye-witnesses' evidence and medical report as to cause death should be accepted.
respondent_arguments: There is contradiction between the medical evidence and the eye-witnesses' evidence, hence their evidence cannot be believed.
court_reasoning: If really the body of the deceased was thrown into the river there can be no possibility of blood still coming out from the nostrils at the time of postmortem as also the presence of semen, being noticed by the doctor.

The High Court, therefore, was justified in coming to the conclusion that it is most likely that the incident in question must have happened early in the morning on the bank of the river without being noticed by anybody and the eye- witnesses were deposing falsely.
